result.document_summary: Boston city FAQ for tenants explaining the Housing Stability Notification Act ordinance, which requires landlords to give tenants a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources and notify the city when ending a tenancy.
result.notes: Single instrument extracted: Boston's Housing Stability Notification Act, a notice-procedure ordinance for terminating tenancies. It does not limit eviction causes, so it is categorized under just_cause_eviction as the closest in-scope category (eviction notice requirements). Effective date taken from the FAQ's statement; the ordinance citation is given as Sec. 10-11.7, which the document shows for enforcement. Lowered confidence because it is a notice requirement rather than a true just-cause regime.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act - notice of tenants' rights and notice to city before ending a tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord or foreclosing owner ending a tenancy must deliver a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources to the tenant at the same time as the Notice to Quit or non-renewal notice, and send a copy of that notice with a Certificate of Compliance/Service to the City's Office of Housing Stability. Violations draw a warning, then $300 per day, but do not halt the eviction process.
rules.key_value: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources delivered with Notice to Quit; copy to Office of Housing Stability
rules.citation: Boston City Ordinances § 10-11.7 (Housing Stability Notification Act)
rules.quoted_span: The HSNA becomes effective on November 6, 2020.
rules.coverage_text: All landlords and foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston.

rules.exemptions_text: Only residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, and non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities are exempt.
rules.interaction: The requirements cannot be waived by lease or contract; violation does not halt the eviction process.
